tagline.text: A cream-sand beach about 2 km long, lined with palm trees, in Pagudpud at the northern tip of Luzon

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–5,000 (per person per night, lodging and meals, excluding transport)

children.text: Saud Beach is a cream-colored sand beach about 2 km long in Pagudpud, at the northern end of Luzon. Palm trees and blue water stretch along the shore, and it is far quieter than better-known resort destinations. It pairs well with the Bangui windmills, Blue Lagoon, and Kabigan Falls on a 2-day, 1-night trip.

Saud Beach is in Barangay Saud, Pagudpud, Ilocos Norte. It sits at the very top of Luzon, on a coast that faces the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea). According to local guides, the beach runs about
2 km

and the sand is cream-colored. Palm trees line the shore and the water is clear, which has made the beach popular in photos. Wikipedia notes that the Philippines' ninth tourist rest area opened in 2024 near the Apo Idon resort here, and that the windmills of neighboring Bangui can be seen in the distance.
Pagudpud is about
72 km
north of the provincial capital Laoag (about 72.5 km according to Wikipedia) and about
558 km

from Manila. Because it is so far, it is not as crowded as Boracay or Cebu, and many visitors report that on weekdays most of the beach is nearly empty. The flip side is that a day trip from Manila is not realistic; plan at least 2 days and 1 night so you are not rushed by travel time. The village behind the beach mixes simple homestays and beachfront resorts, so you can choose by budget. Flying shortens the trip a lot, since Laoag Airport is about 1 hour from Manila, but you still need roughly 1.5 hours by road from the airport to Pagudpud. If you have time, you can take an overnight bus from Manila, arrive at dawn and use the whole day, or spend a day in Laoag seeing Vigan or Paoay first before heading north. Either way, plan the schedule including the trip back.

Saud Beach alone is not enough to justify the trip. To the north are Blue Lagoon (Maira-ira Cove), Kabigan Falls, Patapat Viaduct, and Bantay Abot Cave; to the south are the Bangui windmills, Kapurpurawan Rock, and Cape Bojeador Lighthouse. Local tricycle drivers bundle each direction into a half-day tour, so the most common plan is one day resting on the beach and one day touring. For the wider area, see the
Pagudpud
entry as well.

This is a northern coast that is strongly affected by waves and weather. The sea is calmest from March to May, but from June the southwest monsoon (habagat) builds the waves, and in September and October it is said to be rough enough to produce rip currents. Guides also say lifeguards are not posted at all times, so judge swimming conditions yourself and do not go deeper than your knees on rough days. On entry there is an environmental fee of about
(it varies by source), and beach cottages and lodging are charged separately. Prices change often, so confirm locally.

blocks.title: A cream-sand beach about 2 km long

children.text: Cream-colored sand runs for a long stretch under the palm trees, and the beach is pleasant just to walk. In the early morning it is empty and good for photos, and in the evening the sun sets over the western sea. The sand is fine and soft, good for walking barefoot, but it gets hot at midday, so bring sandals.

The beach faces west, so it is a good place to watch the sunset. On clear days the windmills of neighboring Bangui are said to be visible in the distance, making a northern-Luzon scene together with the sunset.

30 minutes
from Saud Beach by tricycle. Some sources list an entrance fee of about
per person. The water is bright and the waves are often fairly gentle, making it good for swimming and photos.

This coastal viaduct links the mountains and the sea and passes above Pasaleng Bay. It is on the north tour, the views are good, and many people get out briefly to take photos.
On the south tour you see the 20 wind turbines lined up along the sea, then walk to Kapurpurawan Rock, where white limestone is carved into wave-like shapes (entrance about

15-minute
walk). A stop at Cape Bojeador Lighthouse (entrance about

Bagnet (fried pork), Ilocos longganisa, and Ilocos empanada are the classic dishes. At homestays or small eateries a meal costs about

items.title: 2 days, 1 night
items.subtitle: The beach plus north and south tours

children.text: If you arrived on the overnight bus from Manila, take a tricycle from Pagudpud town to Saud Beach, drop your bags, and walk the beach in the morning.
Have Ilocos food for lunch at your lodging or a beachside restaurant.
Hire a tricycle for the north tour (Blue Lagoon, Kabigan Falls, Patapat Viaduct, Bantay Abot Cave).
Return to the beach, watch the sunset, and have dinner.
Get up early to swim and take photos on the quiet beach.
Do the south tour to the Bangui windmills, Kapurpurawan Rock, and Cape Bojeador Lighthouse, then head to Laoag and on home.

A tricycle usually carries up to 3 people on tours, and the hire price is negotiated. If you are flying out of Laoag, add at least 2 hours for the trip from Pagudpud to the airport and finish the last tour early.

items.title: A day resting on the beach
items.subtitle: A relaxed rest day

children.text: After breakfast, walk and swim on the beach.
Rent a shaded cottage and rest.
When the sun gets lower, swim again or walk along the sand.
Watch the sunset and have dinner.
GV Florida, Partas, Viron, and others run buses toward Pagudpud or Laoag from the Cubao, Pasay, and Sampaloc terminals. Departures are usually in the evening around
and the ride is listed at
10–12 hours
Fares are listed from about
for a regular bus to about
for a luxury sleeper. Get off in Pagudpud town and take a tricycle to the beach.
Schedules and fares change, so confirm when you book.
Most buses arrive around dawn, so ask your lodging in advance about early check-in.
The flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Laoag (LAO) takes about
1 hour
. Guides list Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific on the route, with one-way fares from about
when booked early to
or more at short notice.
From Laoag to Pagudpud takes about
1.5–2 hours
by bus or van, listed at about

items.title: The last stretch to the beach

children.text: From Pagudpud town to Saud Beach is about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle, listed at about
per vehicle.
A tricycle for a tour is listed at about
per vehicle (up to 3 people). Confirm the route and price before you leave.
The best time to swim, when the sea is calmest, is
March–May

. This is the end of the dry season, so it is hot and the sun is strong; take care with sun protection. Wikipedia's climate data shows December to April as relatively dry and July–August as the wettest months.
From
June–August
the southwest monsoon arrives and waves begin to build, and in
September–October
guides say the surf is rough with rip currents.
September–December
is also typhoon season in northern Luzon, so check the forecast and leave room in your schedule.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Homestays 50–100 m inland from the beach (EJ's, Cathy's, Vangie's, and others) are the cheapest, listed at about
per night. Right on the beach are resorts such as Hakuna Matata, Evangeline's Beach Resort, Apo Idon, Villa Manuela, and Saud Beach Resort and Hotel, at about
or more per night. Near Blue Lagoon, GlennMark's Homestay and Jay Henry Transient Beach House are known. Book early for peak-season weekends and holidays.

Be sure to try Ilocos dishes such as bagnet, Ilocos longganisa, and empanada. Places known for meals include Emohruo Beach Restobar inside Evangeline's and La Cocina de Consuelo. Guides say cash is essential and ATMs are few and often unreliable, so bring plenty of cash from Manila or Laoag.
Plan at least 2 days and 1 night. Taking the overnight bus from Manila cuts down travel time.
Carry plenty of cash. ATMs are few and often out of order.
Split the tours into half days: north (Blue Lagoon, Kabigan Falls, and others) and south (Bangui windmills and others).
Wear non-slip shoes for the Kabigan Falls trek.
Time your tours so you are back at the beach for sunset.
Early morning is the quietest and best for photos.
Swim only in shallow water on days when the waves are gentle, and always keep children with an adult.
Agree on the tricycle fare along with the route before you get in.
Prices differ a lot between the beachfront and inland. If the sea matters more than a pool, an inland homestay is enough. A beachfront resort, however, lets you step straight onto the sand.
Lifeguards are not posted at all times and rip currents occur in September–October, so do not swim in deep water on days with strong waves.
September–December is typhoon season in northern Luzon. Check the weather forecast.
Some reviews say certain resort areas charge separate usage or cottage fees, so check before you enter.
Fares and schedules change. Check the latest information locally.
ATMs can be unreliable, so bring enough cash.
Trails to places like Kabigan Falls are slippery in the rainy season, so do not push on.

The
Patapat Viaduct

About
30 minutes to 1 hour
south, the
Bangui Windmills

The
Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
